html:
The Indo-Pakistani War of 1971 was a thirteen-day war from 3 to 16 December in which India defeated Pakistan and Bangladesh became independent.

It followed months of crisis. Ten million refugees from the genocide in East Pakistan were in India, the Mukti Bahini was fighting, and Indira Gandhi was ready for war. Pakistan struck first on 3 December with air raids on Indian airfields. India replied on both fronts.

In the East, Indian troops and the Mukti Bahini bypassed strongholds and closed on Dhaka. On 16 December General A. A. K. Niazi signed the surrender to Lieutenant General Jagjit Singh Aurora, and some 93,000 Pakistani soldiers and officials became prisoners. In the West the fighting ended in a ceasefire on 17 December.

The United States sent a task force led by the carrier USS Enterprise into the Bay of Bengal in a show of support for Pakistan, and the Soviets sent ships behind it, under the treaty with India. The war broke Pakistan in two, made India the leading power of South Asia, and brought down Yahya Khan.
sum: The Indo-Pakistani War of 1971 was a thirteen-day war from 3 to 16 December in which India defeated Pakistan and Bangladesh became independent.
